text:
The Rangers' goaltending has been the story of their autumn, and not only because of the starter. James Reimer's comeback ended with his contract terminated after he cleared waivers, Dylan Garand has been a regular in the crease, and Joonas Korpisalo is back from a long stint on injured reserve. Igor Shesterkin's last four starts were sharp: a .926 save percentage and 4.0 goals saved above expected. Korpisalo made 29 saves in a 3-1 win in Calgary on Wednesday.

Here's the thing the 11-8-1 record hides. New York has been a good process team, with 53.8% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) and 55% over the last ten, and it has scored about 8.5 fewer goals than those chances deserved. We'd call that encouraging rather than worrying.

The Mika Zibanejad, Alexis Lafrenière and Gabe Perreault line has been the engine, outscoring opponents 8-4 with 56% of the chances, and Zibanejad scored twice on Wednesday. The J.T. Miller line with Pavel Dorofeyev and Tye Kartye has dominated the chances (61%) without the goals to show for it, 4-7. Kartye, who arrived from Seattle, is getting called a building block in New York.

Our numbers give the Rangers a 58% chance at the playoffs, projecting about 94 points. What to watch: whether the Miller line's chances start going in, and who settles in net.
